# Projected Evaluation Scorecard

**PROJECTED — not measured.** SPEC v1.5 § 8.2, as of 2026-11-21. Generated by [build_scorecard.py](build_scorecard.py) from [scorecard.yaml](scorecard.yaml) and validated by [scripts/test_scorecard.py](../../scripts/test_scorecard.py). Each cell rates a stack against an E-dimension pass criterion (SPEC § 8) from the documentation, the local evidence in this repository and the design. A measured run supersedes any cell.

## 1. Headline findings

- Modern engineering practice is not where the legacy stacks fall short. The cube is projected to meet CI/CD, partition rollover and near-real-time freshness, at the cost of a SQL Server adapter and a cache-clear cadence. The Tabular model meets rollover, and meets CI/CD except for manual Copilot setup. (S1/E4, S1/E5, S1/E6, S2/E5, S2/E6)
- Calendar time intelligence favors the proprietary engines. MDX and DAX anchor on the calendar, and Tableau does so with a parameter. The SQL-native metric views anchor on the last date with data and cannot list members without facts, the only projected E1 shortfall. (S1/E1, S2/E1, S3/E1, S4/E1)
- Governance and speed trade off in the lakehouse layer. Unity Catalog enforces the security rules once for every consumer, but a governed metric view cannot be materialized, so the fast path and the secure path are separate deployments. (S4/E3, S4/E8)
- Semantic-layer-as-code is universal. All four stacks are generated or linted from Git and validated by committed suites; YAML has no monopoly. (S1/E5, S2/E5, S3/E5, S4/E5)
- Most of the scorecard is low-confidence by construction. 26 of the 36 cells rest on design inference or on an unverified vendor behavior, and performance, freshness latency and agent accuracy stay open for every stack until a measured run. (S1/E3, S2/E3, S3/E3, S4/E3, S2/E4, S2/E7, S4/E7)

## 3. Marketing claims (projected verdicts)

| Claim | Statement | Verdict | Evidence · confidence | Cells |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MC-01 | OLAP cubes cannot deliver near-real-time data. | **Refuted with cost** | DI · Low | S1/E4, S2/E4 |
| MC-02 | Legacy semantic models cannot be managed with modern CI/CD. | **Refuted** | DI · Low | S1/E5, S2/E5 |
| MC-03 | Cubes do not scale to high-volume, granular data. | **Inconclusive** | DI · Low | S1/E3, S1/E6 |
| MC-04 | Complex time intelligence and semi-additive logic require a proprietary calculation engine. | **Refuted with cost** | DI · Low | S1/E1, S2/E1, S3/E1, S4/E1 |
| MC-05 | AI agents require a modern, SQL-native semantic layer to answer business questions accurately. | **Inconclusive** | DI · Low | S1/E7, S2/E7, S3/E7, S4/E7 |
| MC-06 | Self-service exploration beyond predefined reports requires a lakehouse-native semantic layer. | **Refuted** | DI · Low | S1/E2, S2/E2, S4/E2 |
| MC-07 | Only a lakehouse catalog can enforce governance consistently across BI and AI consumers. | **Refuted with cost** | DI · Low | S1/E8, S2/E8, S3/E8, S4/E8 |
| MC-08 | Semantic-layer-as-code is unique to YAML-defined metric layers. | **Refuted** | LV · High | S1/E5, S2/E5, S3/E5, S4/E5 |

**MC-01 — Refuted with cost.** The cube serves the current month from a ROLAP hot partition, so new rows are visible without processing. Over Databricks this costs a SQL Server adapter (B-09) and an explicit cache clear (B-10). The Tabular engine's hybrid partition needs no workaround. *Confirmed or overturned by:* S1 sentinel-trip p95 within 15 minutes with the cache-clear cadence recorded.

**MC-02 — Refuted.** The cube is generated from Python into ASSL, deployed and processed over XMLA, and gated on oracle reconciliation by a GitHub workflow, with no manual step. The Power BI gaps are vendor features (verified answers), not the legacy engine. *Confirmed or overturned by:* An unattended S1 deploy-process-reconcile-promote run from a Git push.

**MC-03 — Inconclusive.** The design (about 80M trips in 24 monthly MOLAP partitions, per-month distinct-count groups, automated rollover) gives no reason to expect failure. Scale is a measurement, and nothing has been measured. *Confirmed or overturned by:* S1 E3 percentiles at concurrency 10 and two clean rollovers on the full data.

**MC-04 — Refuted with cost.** The SQL-native layer handles semi-additive and period-to-date logic with window measures, without a proprietary engine. But it anchors on data, not the calendar (B-07), and cannot list members without facts (B-08). Matching the SPEC needs a calendar × member dense source at a cost of days × members rows per dimension. The proprietary engines (MDX, DAX) meet the definition directly. *Confirmed or overturned by:* S4 window-metric reconciliation confirming B-07, set against S1 and S2 matching the same cells.

**MC-05 — Inconclusive.** Agent accuracy is unmeasured. Structurally, the SQL-native layer's semantic gaps (B-07, B-08) pass straight into agent answers. The legacy cube is reachable only through the common harness (B-04), not denied to agents. *Confirmed or overturned by:* Per-lane accuracy, pass@3 and consistency for all four stacks on the 70 questions.

**MC-06 — Refuted.** The legacy engines express all 70 questions, including every D-level self-service question, against unchanged models. The lakehouse-native layer is the one that falls short (Q-N-S2-D4, B-08). *Confirmed or overturned by:* E2 runs with zero model changes on S1 and S2.

**MC-07 — Refuted with cost.** Each BI layer enforces the SPEC § 10 rules for its BI and agent consumers, but the rules are written three more times, once per layer: the consistency cost the claim points at. The catalog enforces them once, but at the price of acceleration (B-01) and pending V-28. *Confirmed or overturned by:* All four stacks pass the 24 restricted questions per role in every lane.

**MC-08 — Refuted.** Every stack is defined as code in Git and validated in CI: ASSL and MDX (S1), TMDL and DAX (S2), and .tds files valid against Tableau's official XSD (S3), next to the YAML metric views (S4). All four are generated or linted by committed tooling, and their suites pass locally. *Confirmed or overturned by:* Each stack's model round-trips from Git to its server and back without manual editing.

## 4. Cells

### 4.1 E1 Metric correctness

Pass criterion: 100% of cells within tolerance (§ 9.3)

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The MDX calculation script implements every metric with the SPEC semantics. LastNonEmpty serves W-M2. Period-to-date metrics anchor on the calendar end of the period, so B-07 does not arise. Same-period-last-year uses a key-based member property instead of ParallelPeriod, which misplaces leap-day anchors (V-36). The many-to-many dimension deduplicates W-C1 totals, and dimension members exist without facts, so B-08 does not arise. The model is well-formed and every reference resolves, but no MDX has executed.
- Depends on pending verification: V-40
- Sources: V-35, V-36, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [test_ssas_md.py](../../scripts/test_ssas_md.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: All 22 metric files reconcile to the oracle on the deployed cube. Watch above all the N-C1 cells for 2024 dates after 28 February and the W-C2 91-day anchor; a mismatch there overturns the cell.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Explicit DAX measures implement the SPEC anchors: the calendar end of the period capped at 2024-12-31, with 29 February mapped to 28 February. Built-in calendar time intelligence cannot serve the composite and hybrid variants (B-14). Measures carry ISCROSSFILTERED guards so the applicability matrix's N cells return blank instead of a repeated total (B-15). Every DAX reference resolves against the TMDL, but no DAX engine ran.
- Boundaries: B-14, B-15
- Sources: V-13, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md), [test_powerbi_tabular.py](../../scripts/test_powerbi_tabular.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: All 22 metric queries reconcile in the Import, Direct Lake and DirectQuery variants. An N cell that returns a value, or a YTD cell that disagrees on a sparse member, overturns the cell.

**S3 Tableau — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: All 22 metric plans reproduce the oracle on the fixtures through the VizQL Data Service emulator. The emulator restates each Tableau calculation in SQL, so Tableau's own evaluation is inferred, not shown. Semi-additive stock needs an EXCLUDE level-of-detail pattern that names every non-date dimension (B-05). Period-to-date metrics need an As-of Date parameter and one query per anchor, which keeps them calendar-anchored (B-17).
- Boundaries: B-05, B-17
- Depends on pending verification: V-52
- Sources: V-47, V-48, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [vds_emulator.py](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/tools/vds_emulator.py), [test_tableau.py](../../scripts/test_tableau.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Live VizQL Data Service reconciliation of all 22 metrics. A W-M2 value after an SCD2 change, or a period-to-date value read with the parameter override, that differs from the oracle overturns the cell.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Partial** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Non-window measures are exact on the real data: 64 of 65 non-window queries match, and the one difference is B-08. Window measures anchor a coarser group on the last date with data, not the calendar end of the period (B-07, V-30). Members without facts are unreachable (B-08). The exposure was counted on B0.
- Holds and fails: Holds for all 17 metric files without a window measure: the emulator reproduces every committed B0 cell. It fails for N-C1 and N-C2 month × member rows of sparse members: 12 rows with an early anchor and 27 absent rows across Staten Island, EWR, the Unknown payment type and vendor 6.
- Boundaries: B-07, B-08
- Depends on pending verification: V-30
- Sources: V-02, V-30, B-07, B-08, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md), [test_databricks_metric_views.py](../../scripts/test_databricks_metric_views.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Workspace reconciliation of the window metrics. If the sparse-member cells match the oracle, V-30 is false and the cell rises to Meets; if they differ exactly as counted, B-07 is confirmed.

### 4.2 E2 Self-service depth

Pass criterion: 100% correct; zero model changes during the run

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: All 70 questions are expressed in MDX against one unchanged cube. Members are listed independently of facts, so the dimension-driven questions (Q-W-S2-P, Q-N-S2-D4) return the oracle's full member lists. Every hierarchy, measure and property resolves, and output columns equal the oracle headers.
- Depends on pending verification: V-40
- Sources: [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [test_ssas_md.py](../../scripts/test_ssas_md.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: All 70 questions reconcile through Excel or MDX with zero model changes during the run.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: All 70 questions are DAX queries against one model per dataset. Questions that list every member iterate the dimension, so Q-N-S2-D4 returns all seven payment codes. References resolve and headers match the oracle, but no DAX has executed.
- Sources: [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md), [test_powerbi_tabular.py](../../scripts/test_powerbi_tabular.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: All 70 questions reconcile in each storage-mode variant with zero model changes.

**S3 Tableau — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: All 70 question plans reproduce the oracle on the fixtures through the emulator. The query service has no query composition, so drill paths query each grain and select client-side (B-16). Period-to-date questions set the As-of parameter per anchor (B-17). Dimension-driven questions take members from dimension-only queries and match the oracle row for row.
- Boundaries: B-16, B-17
- Depends on pending verification: V-53
- Sources: V-47, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [test_tableau.py](../../scripts/test_tableau.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: All 70 plans reconcile against a live site, including the presence-measure handling of unmatched members (V-53).

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Partial** (Locally verified, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: The B-08 shortfall is observed on the real data through the emulator and follows from the documented join model, in which the source is the fact (V-03). Window questions are safe only when the anchor is selected outside the window (V-31); the committed queries do so, but self-service clients may not.
- Holds and fails: All 70 questions are answered by MEASURE() queries over unchanged views. Q-N-S2-D4 cannot list payment codes without 2024 trips (5 of the oracle's 7 rows, observed on B0). Q-W-S2-P depends on every month having facts.
- Boundaries: B-08
- Sources: V-03, B-08, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md), [test_databricks_metric_views.py](../../scripts/test_databricks_metric_views.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Workspace run of all 70 queries: Q-N-S2-D4 returns 5 rows and every other question matches the oracle (window questions included).

### 4.3 E3 Query performance

Pass criterion: Warm p95 ≤ 2 s for `P`; warm p95 ≤ 5 s for `D1`–`D4` and `AH` at concurrency 10; cold latency reported

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Monthly MOLAP partitions and per-month distinct-count measure groups bound the scans. Aggregations are designed from the E3 query log, not in advance. The ROLAP hot partition reads Databricks through SQL Server (B-09), so its latency depends on PolyBase pushdown (V-39). The raw-SQL floor is 1.08 s or less for every question.
- Expected range: MOLAP P questions well under 2 s warm. The N-C1, N-C2 and W-C2 cells (EXISTING date sets, StrToMember) are the formula-engine risk at concurrency 10. Hot-partition queries add the PolyBase hop.
- Boundaries: B-09
- Depends on pending verification: V-39
- Sources: B-09, V-39, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [ORACLE_REPORT.md](../../01-spec/oracle/ORACLE_REPORT.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Warm p95 at concurrency 10 within 2 s (P) and 5 s (D1-D4), measured with and without usage-based aggregations and with the hot partition populated.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Not assessable** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: No workaround is involved, so the measurement alone decides. The expected range favors Import and Direct Lake. DirectQuery inherits S4-like live latency plus DAX-to-SQL translation.
- Expected range: Import and Direct Lake: P and D questions expected well inside the targets (VertiPaq over about 80M trips is far inside the F64 guardrails). DirectQuery: each DAX query becomes one or more SQL queries on serverless SQL, so concurrency-10 latency is that of the warehouse and is not projectable.
- Sources: V-12, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md), [ORACLE_REPORT.md](../../01-spec/oracle/ORACLE_REPORT.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Warm p95 per variant at concurrency 1 and 10; the DirectQuery variant decides whether S2 needs a workaround.

**S3 Tableau — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Live queries compile to SQL on Databricks with relationship join culling. The pervasive WWI security filter always joins City. The lack of query composition (B-16) and the per-anchor parameter (B-17) multiply calls; the extract variant moves the work to Hyper.
- Expected range: Single-query P questions run at live serverless SQL latency plus the service overhead. Drill-path and multi-anchor questions issue several calls (12 for Q-N-C1-P), so their end-to-end time is several round trips.
- Boundaries: B-16, B-17
- Sources: B-16, B-17, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [ORACLE_REPORT.md](../../01-spec/oracle/ORACLE_REPORT.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Warm p95 per question, counting every call of a plan, at concurrency 1 and 10, for live and extract variants.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: A metric view compiles to the SQL the oracle already runs and joins only what the query needs. Acceleration exists only in the accelerated profile, because materialization is impossible over ABAC-governed sources (B-01). The fast path and the governed path are therefore different deployments.
- Expected range: Governed profile: live serverless SQL over clustered Delta, near the raw-SQL floor (1.08 s or less on 4 vCPU DuckDB) plus warehouse overhead. Accelerated profile: cube-grain questions served from the materializations.
- Boundaries: B-01
- Sources: B-01, V-06, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md), [ORACLE_REPORT.md](../../01-spec/oracle/ORACLE_REPORT.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Warm p95 at concurrency 10 for both profiles, and which questions the engine serves from materializations.

### 4.4 E4 Data freshness

Pass criterion: p95 ≤ 15 minutes

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The current month is a ROLAP hot partition, so new gold rows are visible without processing. Real-time ROLAP cannot be notified through external tables (B-10), so freshness relies on an explicit cache clear, and every read crosses the adapter (B-09).
- Expected range: Pipeline commit latency plus one ClearCache and a ROLAP read through PolyBase: minutes, inside 15 minutes if the poller clears the cache at least every few minutes.
- Boundaries: B-09, B-10
- Depends on pending verification: V-39
- Sources: V-37, B-09, B-10, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [partition_rollover.py](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/jobs/partition_rollover.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Sentinel trips visible in MDX within 15 minutes at p95, with the cache-clear cadence recorded.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Not assessable** (Documented, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: Each NYC variant has a documented live path: a hybrid real-time partition, Direct Lake reframing, or DirectQuery. No workaround is needed, so only the latency measurement can rate the cell.
- Expected range: Hybrid NYC model: the real-time DirectQuery partition shows rows as soon as Databricks commits them. Direct Lake: mirroring latency (seconds to minutes) plus automatic reframing. DirectQuery: live.
- Sources: V-12, V-13, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Sentinel trip p95 per variant; the Direct Lake mirroring delay is the uncertain term.

**S3 Tableau — Partial** (Documented, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: Incremental extract refresh on the pickup timestamp is documented (V-50). Sub-15-minute schedules are a site setting, not a product guarantee.
- Holds and fails: The live variant shows committed rows on the next query. The extract variant is only as fresh as its last incremental refresh, so it meets 15 minutes only with a refresh schedule of that frequency.
- Expected range: Live variant at pipeline latency; extract variant at its refresh interval plus refresh duration.
- Sources: V-50, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [refresh.py](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/jobs/refresh.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Sentinel trip p95 for both variants at the configured extract schedule.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The metric view adds no latency of its own over Delta. Freshness and acceleration trade off across the two profiles (B-01), and the platform's freshness pipeline is not measured here.
- Expected range: Governed profile: pipeline commit latency, because every query is live. Accelerated profile: queries the materializations cover may serve data up to the hourly refresh old.
- Boundaries: B-01
- Sources: B-01, V-06, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Sentinel trip p95 in both profiles, and whether materialized queries return the sentinel before refresh.

### 4.5 E5 CI/CD

Pass criterion: Zero manual steps; rollback by redeploying the previous commit

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: A push runs lint, then deploy and process over XMLA, then the P-question reconciliation gate, then promotion on main, with no manual step in the flow. Deployment runs on a self-hosted Windows runner, and the engine's acceptance of the generated ASSL is untested (V-40).
- Depends on pending verification: V-40
- Sources: V-40, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [s1-ssas-md.yml](../../.github/workflows/s1-ssas-md.yml)
- Confirmed or overturned by: A model change flows to prod unattended, and redeploying the previous commit rolls it back.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Partial** (Documented, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: Verified answers are not supported by Git, REST or deployment pipelines (V-43), so a change touching them needs a manual step. RLS models force the CI gate onto XMLA with a stored service-principal secret (B-13).
- Holds and fails: Model, refresh and reconciliation are automated (fabric-cicd, enhanced refresh, XMLA gate). Copilot verified answers, AI-instruction sync and per-environment connections and role membership are manual.
- Boundaries: B-12, B-13
- Sources: V-17, V-43, B-12, B-13, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md), [verified_answers.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/copilot/verified_answers.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: A model-only change flows unattended; a verified-answer change cannot.

**S3 Tableau — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: A push runs lint, publish of the live and extract data sources through the REST API, the P-question gate, and promotion. Environment values are injected at publish time and nothing environment-specific is committed.
- Depends on pending verification: V-52
- Sources: V-52, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [s3-tableau.yml](../../.github/workflows/s3-tableau.yml)
- Confirmed or overturned by: A calculation change flows to prod unattended and the gate passes.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: A push runs lint and tests, then bundle deploy, the deploy job and the P-question gate in test, then promotion, authenticated by workload identity federation with no stored token (V-33). The bundle syncs the oracle answers from the same commit (V-32). The jobs have not run on a workspace.
- Sources: V-32, V-33, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md), [s4-metric-views.yml](../../.github/workflows/s4-metric-views.yml)
- Confirmed or overturned by: A YAML change flows to prod unattended; the gate fails when a planted wrong measure is pushed.

### 4.6 E6 Partition and refresh automation

Pass criterion: Two consecutive simulated rollovers succeed with E1 still passing

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The rollover script reads the current partitions and runs one transactional batch: create and process the closed month, re-slice the hot partition, retire months beyond 24, then clear the cache. Plans for two consecutive months are tested locally, and partition coverage of every trip is checked on the fixtures. Enterprise edition is required for more than three partitions (V-35).
- Depends on pending verification: V-40
- Sources: V-35, [partition_rollover.py](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/jobs/partition_rollover.py), [test_ssas_md.py](../../scripts/test_ssas_md.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Two consecutive simulated rollovers on the server with E1 still passing.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Meets** (Documented, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: The hybrid refresh policy keeps 24 monthly partitions, refreshes the last 3 days incrementally and adds the real-time partition. The service creates, merges and retires partitions on each applyRefreshPolicy refresh (V-13).
- Sources: V-13, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Two consecutive simulated month closes leave exactly 24 monthly partitions with E1 still passing.

**S3 Tableau — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The NYC extract refreshes incrementally on the pickup timestamp. A monthly full refresh with a rolling 24-month relative-date extract filter retires the month that left the window. The live variant has no partitions to manage.
- Depends on pending verification: V-52
- Sources: V-50, V-52, [refresh.py](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/jobs/refresh.py)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Two simulated rollovers leave exactly 24 months in the extract with E1 still passing.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: The semantic layer holds no partitions: the views read clustered Delta live, and retention beyond 24 months is a platform delete. Materializations refresh on their schedule, incrementally where possible (V-29). Nothing in S4 needs a rollover step.
- Sources: V-29, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: After two simulated rollovers on the platform, E1 passes in both profiles with no S4 change.

### 4.7 E7 AI agent accessibility

Pass criterion: Reported per lane: accuracy, pass@3, 3-of-3 consistency, median latency

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: There is no native assistant (B-04), so the agent harness is the only lane. Its MCP server exists only as specification (SPEC § 11), so no accuracy can be projected beyond parity of metadata.
- Expected range: Common-harness lane only, over XMLA/MDX. Accuracy depends on the agent writing MDX against a cube whose metadata comes from the same glossary as every other stack.
- Boundaries: B-04
- Sources: B-04, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Harness-lane accuracy, pass@3 and 3-of-3 consistency on the 70 questions.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Not assessable** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Agent accuracy is a measurement. The linguistic schema format for synonyms is undocumented (V-45), and verified answers need manual setup (B-12).
- Expected range: Copilot lane over a model with AI instructions, verified answers and synonyms, plus the harness lane over XMLA/DAX. Calendar-anchored measures avoid the B-07 errors an agent would inherit in S4.
- Depends on pending verification: V-45
- Sources: V-13, V-45, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Copilot and harness accuracy, pass@3 and consistency on the 70 questions.

**S3 Tableau — Meets with workaround** (Documented, Medium confidence)

- Rationale: Tableau Agent indexes captions and the first 150 characters of descriptions only (V-14), and there is no synonym property (B-18). Multi-call question plans (B-16) are hard for an agent to discover unaided.
- Expected range: Tableau Agent lane plus the harness lane over the query service. Synonyms are appended to descriptions, and 5 of 69 visible fields carry synonyms beyond the 150 indexed characters.
- Boundaries: B-18
- Sources: V-14, B-16, B-18, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Agent and harness accuracy on the 70 questions, split by whether the needed synonym is inside the indexed prefix.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Partial** (Documented, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Agent metadata is first-class in YAML 1.1 (V-01, V-08), but semantic gaps in the layer pass straight through to every agent.
- Holds and fails: Genie and the harness read rich metadata (comment, display_name, synonyms, format) on every member. No lane can answer exactly the questions B-07 and B-08 affect, and a date filter pushed into a window-measure query truncates the window (V-31).
- Expected range: Strong metadata coverage. The accuracy ceiling is set by Q-N-S2-D4, by sparse-member period-to-date questions, and by how often agents place date filters inside window queries.
- Boundaries: B-07, B-08
- Depends on pending verification: V-31
- Sources: V-01, V-08, V-31, B-07, B-08, [METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/databricks-metric-views/METRIC_VIEWS_GUIDE.md)
- Confirmed or overturned by: Genie and harness accuracy, with the share of window questions where the agent filtered inside the window.

### 4.8 E8 Governance parity

Pass criterion: Restricted identities see exactly the oracle's restricted results in every lane

**S1 SSAS MD — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Roles restrict City to the Southeast territory with visual totals, and grant an empty allowed set on inventory. Restricted expected answers now exist for every P and D1 question. If an empty allowed set raises an error instead of returning NULL (V-38), the cell-security fallback returns #N/A and differs from the oracle.
- Depends on pending verification: V-38
- Sources: V-38, [SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/ssas-md/SSAS_MD_GUIDE.md), [restricted](../../01-spec/oracle/expected/restricted)
- Confirmed or overturned by: The 24 restricted questions reconcile per role in the harness and through Excel.

**S2 Power BI / Tabular — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Model RLS roles implement both SPEC § 10 rules, and the dropoff role stays unrestricted. Role reconciliation in CI uses XMLA with an effective identity, because service principals cannot be role members and executeQueries refuses them on RLS models (B-13).
- Boundaries: B-13
- Sources: V-41, V-42, B-13, [POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/powerbi-tabular/POWERBI_TABULAR_GUIDE.md), [restricted](../../01-spec/oracle/expected/restricted)
- Confirmed or overturned by: The 24 restricted questions reconcile per role in each variant, through reports and Copilot.

**S3 Tableau — Meets** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: Data source filters with ISMEMBEROF are evaluated for the querying identity. The territory filter is pervasive because it references City, so it also narrows the City member list. The stock filter denies inventory, and the NYC filter is scoped to Trips so dropoff zones stay browsable.
- Depends on pending verification: V-53
- Sources: V-49, V-53, [TABLEAU_GUIDE.md](../../02-implementations/bi-layer/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md), [restricted](../../01-spec/oracle/expected/restricted)
- Confirmed or overturned by: The 24 restricted questions reconcile per role through the query service and Tableau Agent.

**S4 Databricks Metric Views — Meets with workaround** (Design inference, Low confidence)

- Rationale: With the SPEC § 10 row filters on the source tables, the emulator reproduces the restricted oracle answers for the 15 role questions without a window measure, on fixtures and on B0. The remaining 9 window questions are inferred. That ABAC policies filter the querying principal through a metric view is unverified (V-28), and the governed profile forgoes materialization (B-01).
- Boundaries: B-01
- Depends on pending verification: V-28
- Sources: V-16, V-27, V-28, B-01, [test_databricks_metric_views.py](../../scripts/test_databricks_metric_views.py), [restricted](../../01-spec/oracle/expected/restricted)
- Confirmed or overturned by: The 24 restricted questions reconcile per role through Genie and the harness in the governed profile.
